title: Lake Van temple basalt brought from 350 miles away
summary: Matt tells of Lake Van temple basalt brought from 350 miles away, about ancient at Lake Van region sites (Ayanis, Kef Kalesi, Çavuştepe), Turkey, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Lake Van region sites (Ayanis, Kef Kalesi, Çavuştepe), Turkey

tellings.quote: some of the balt that they used in this this construction is considered to possibly come from 350 miles away

plain: A researcher named only as Matt, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in an episode about something big happening around 12,000 BC, talks about ancient sites near Lake Van in eastern Turkey, such as Ayanis, Kef Kalesi and Çavuştepe. He says some of the basalt, a dark, heavy volcanic rock, used to build them may have come from 350 miles away. If so, the ancient builders were moving huge stones over very long distances.
